name: The Fool
title: The Fool
age: Looks ancient, but leaps like a child

origin.birthplace: Claims he was born "on a Tuesday, on the back of a joke"
origin.socialStatus: A host with no official role; entertains the guests
origin.profession: An old court jester who says he served kings no one remembers

appearance.face: A wrinkled face painted white, a red smile wider than his mouth
appearance.hairAndEyes: Shaggy white hair under his cap; one eye blue, the other amber
appearance.clothing: Worn motley patched with scraps of other people's cloaks; a cap with bells; a staff with a carved wooden head that looks like him
appearance.build: Thin, wiry, nimble; jumps, dances, sits right on the table
appearance.gestures: Jingles his bells when someone lies (or when he is bored); talks to his staff
appearance.voice: A squeaky, sing-song voice; rhymes, sings, interrupts
appearance.firstImpression: A merry, eccentric old man — you can't tell if he is mad or the only sane one
appearance.artistNotes: His clothes are patched with scraps of every kind of cloth, and he claims each comes from a different country. He carved the staff himself.

backstory.biography: No one remembers when the Fool appeared at the inn. He says he was jester to kings no one remembers, and maybe it's true. He turns every situation into a game and loves chaos and unexpected twists. He laughs even when someone loses everything — but guests who make him laugh for real sometimes get an unexpected gift.
backstory.whyHere: He wants to see what each guest does when the rules shift under their feet.
backstory.secret: How old he is, where he comes from, and whether his madness is real. He probably doesn't know either.

psychology.weakness: Cannot resist chaos, even when it hurts him
psychology.desire: Surprise: someone doing something nobody foresaw
psychology.angers: Dull, predictable people and smug winners
psychology.regret: No one knows. Sometimes he stops laughing and looks at the door
psychology.moralLimits: Does not hurt anyone directly. Chaos is his weapon
psychology.neverWould: Play by the same rules two rounds in a row

behavior.stakes: Loves them, especially absurd ones. Stakes things like "your next laugh"
behavior.deception: A game. Cheats openly and laughs when caught
behavior.alliances: Temporary and absurd. Allies with the weakest to keep it interesting
behavior.whenAttacks: When the game gets boring or someone is too confident
behavior.whenRetreats: Never. He just vanishes and reappears elsewhere
behavior.strategyChange: Boredom, or a player who is too predictable

motives.hiddenGoal: To shake up the order and see who falls
motives.personalReason: Fun. Maybe something older he does not talk about

speech.register: Rhymed, sing-song, full of riddles and nursery rhymes
speech.howLies: Openly and absurdly, so no one knows when he lies
speech.angerAndFear: Rarely. Then he stops laughing and the bells go silent — which is scarier than anything

mechanics.strangeness: His bells ring when someone lies — even when he is standing perfectly still.
mechanics.principle: Play by the same rules two rounds in a row
mechanics.temptation: Cannot resist chaos, even when it hurts him

authorNotes.distinctive: The chaotic jester — no one knows if he is mad or the only sane one in the room.
authorNotes.tunable: How often he flips the course of the evening.

host.presentation: As a harmless mad jester who entertains the guests
host.trueNature: An old eccentric jester; maybe mad, maybe the cleverest in the room
host.neverReveals: His age and his real name
host.rulesAttitude: Flips them, swaps them, laughs at them
host.temptations: Absurd stakes, a second chance, a joke at someone else's expense
host.wouldBreakRules: Always. He has no rules of his own
host.hostingStyle: Leaps between the tables, sits on the table, interrupts rounds with songs. An evening he runs is unpredictable and fast.
host.sampleOffers: "Let's swap hands! Everyone, to the left! My lord, don't sulk, your cards were boring." / "I'll stake my bell against your biggest secret. That's fair!"
host.trueStory: No one knows. Maybe he really was a court jester. Maybe he is just an old man who decided laughter is better than truth.
host.changedRule: Once per evening he shuffles the gifts so that one of them reaches a different person than intended.

lines.text: Oh, a wonderful evening! Someone will get rich, someone will cry, and I shall laugh!
Bravo, bravo! Now let's see how long you keep it!
Ha-ha! Losing suits you better than my cap!
Me? I'm a fool! Blame the clever ones!
An alliance? With me? Ha-ha! You'll regret it, but you'll have fun!
Betrayed you? How wonderful! I'll sing it in a ballad!
Oh, I adore this! Everything on one card, like the good old days!
You! You again! I remember your face — or at least your nose.
Who am I? Ha! Ask my staff, he knows more!
Let's begin! No, wait — let's begin AGAIN! I'm joking. Or am I.
Silent! How fun! My staff is silent too — you two will get along.
Here's a secret! Don't tell anyone. Unless it's funny.
